#### 1. gastric cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.407)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-373753)

**Proposed mechanism:** NPHS1 (HGNC:8009) —DISRUPTS→ Congenital nephrotic syndrome, Finnish type (MONDO:0009732); APC (HGNC:549) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP769); Wnt signaling pathway (WP:WP769) —LEADS_TO→ Gastric cancer (MONDO:0001056). Loss of function in NPHS1 leads to congenital nephrotic syndrome. Concurrently, loss of function in APC disrupts the Wnt signaling pathway, a critical pathway involved in cell proliferation and differentiation, ultimately leading to gastric cancer.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in NPHS1 do not affect Wnt signaling or if APC mutations are found to be unrelated to Wnt signaling dysregulation in gastric cancer, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing a common variant (>5% allele frequency) in NPHS1 or APC that is not associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of Wnt signaling in both nephrotic syndrome and gastric cancer could reveal novel therapeutic targets. For instance, modulating Wnt signaling might offer a strategy for treating aspects of kidney disease or preventing gastric cancer progression.
